references.title: Compilation versus execution
references.body: Build translates and links source into an executable. Run executes that result. An error in either stage is different from a failed exercise check. C Forge explicitly uses C17; printing a language label does not select a dialect.

references.title: Printf conversions used in this course
references.body: %d: int. %u: unsigned int. %ld: long. %f: double (%.2f displays two fractional digits). %c: int holding a character value, including a promoted char. %zu: size_t, including sizeof results. %%: literal %. Argument order and types must match. A mismatch may cause undefined behavior.

references.title: Expected semicolon or closing punctuation
references.body: A diagnostic can point after the actual mistake. Inspect the preceding statement for its closing quote, parenthesis, and semicolon. Repair the first relevant diagnostic, rebuild, then inspect any remaining messages.

references.title: Integer division loses the fractional part
references.body: With two integer operands, / produces an integer quotient, truncating toward zero. Converting that result to double afterward cannot restore a fraction. Convert one operand before division when the desired result is fractional. Always exclude a zero divisor.

references.title: Assignment versus comparison
references.body: = changes an object; == produces a true-or-false integer result. An assignment has a value and may compile inside a condition, so read the intended question and keep warnings visible. C range tests need separate comparisons joined with &&.

references.title: Loop boundaries and progress
references.body: Trace initialization, condition, body, and update. Starting at 0 with i < count includes count small nonnegative values; starting at 1 with i <= count does too. A missing update can prevent termination. continue in a for loop still reaches its update.

references.title: Function prototypes
references.body: A prototype declares the result and parameter types before a call. Its types must agree with the later definition. Use (void) for no parameters in C17.

references.title: Scope and lifetime
references.body: Scope describes where a name can be used. Lifetime describes when the object exists. A returned value can be copied to the caller even though an automatic local object ends when its block exits.
references.example: int next(int value) { int result = value + 1; return result; }

references.title: Array element count
references.body: At a real array object, sizeof array / sizeof array[0] gives the element count. A function array parameter is adjusted to a pointer and needs an explicit count; the same expression there does not give the caller’s length.
references.example: int a[] = {2, 4, 6}; size_t count = sizeof a / sizeof a[0];

references.title: String length and capacity
references.body: strlen counts bytes before NUL in an already valid string. A writable destination needs room for those bytes and one terminator. strlen is not a safe way to validate an arbitrary unterminated buffer.

references.title: Compare strings with strcmp
references.body: strcmp is declared in <string.h>. It compares valid NUL-terminated strings lexicographically and returns a value below zero, zero, or above zero. Do not assume the nonzero result is exactly -1 or 1.

references.title: & and * in expressions
references.body: &object produces its address; *pointer accesses the live object designated by that pointer. In int *p, the star is part of a pointer declaration. NULL must not be dereferenced. A NULL check cannot validate every other address.

references.title: Arrays and pointers differ
references.body: An array contains its elements; a pointer object stores an address. In most expressions an array converts to a pointer to its first element, but sizeof array still measures the actual array. Array parameters adjust to pointers and need a count.
references.example: int a[3] = {1, 2, 3}; int *p = a; /* p has no stored length */

references.title: One-past is a boundary
references.body: Pointer arithmetic can stay within one live array or reach one-past its end. That end pointer may be used as a boundary, but dereferencing it is invalid. NULL + 0 is not a substitute for an array-based end pointer.
references.example: int a[3]; int *end = a + 3; /* never read *end */

references.title: fgets: size, newline, and EOF
references.body: fgets reads at most capacity - 1 characters into the supplied buffer and NUL-terminates a successful read. Newline is retained if read. NULL means no successful line read; ferror distinguishes stream error from EOF. A successful chunk can still be a partial line.
references.example: char line[64]; if (fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin) == NULL) { /* inspect EOF/error */ }

references.title: strtol validation checklist
references.body: Reset errno, use base 10, require at least one digit (end != text), reject ERANGE, inspect leftover text, and enforce application range before use. A zero result alone does not mean failure. Character classification accepts EOF or unsigned-char values.

references.title: Reject a truncated numeric prefix
references.body: A full buffer without newline requires a probe: newline or clean EOF means the line fits exactly; another character means truncation. Drain the remainder and reject the whole line before numeric conversion. fgetc returns int so EOF is distinct from character values.
references.example: int next = fgetc(stdin); /* retain int for EOF */

references.title: Struct member access
references.body: Use object.member for a struct object and pointer->member for a valid pointer to one. Struct assignment copies values; copied pointer members still refer to the same objects.

references.title: Enums and state validation
references.body: Enums name integer constants. A typed enum variable does not replace validation of externally supplied values; reject unknown states before mutation.
references.example: switch (state) { case PENDING: break; case DONE: break; default: /* invalid */ break; }

references.title: Allocation and ownership
references.body: malloc returns uninitialized storage or NULL. A successful returned owning pointer must eventually be freed exactly once. A borrowed alias must not outlive the allocation. Common stack/heap diagrams are implementation models.
references.example: int *p = malloc(3 * sizeof *p); if (p != NULL) { /* initialize and use */ free(p); }

references.title: Safe realloc
references.body: For a nonzero request, failed realloc leaves the original allocation valid. Use a temporary result to preserve the sole owner; check size arithmetic first.
references.example: int *next = realloc(items, bytes); if (next != NULL) items = next;

references.title: Successful opening is not successful saving
references.body: Check fopen, every write, and fclose. Buffered write errors may appear at close. w mode truncates an existing file. Preserve backups when updating important data.
references.example: int ok = fprintf(out, "%d\n", n) >= 0; if (fclose(out) != 0) ok = 0;

references.title: Undefined reference
references.body: A declaration was compiled, but the linker did not find a matching definition. Compile and link the implementation object; verify the exact function name and signature.

references.title: Include guards
references.body: A header guard prevents repeated declarations from being processed multiple times in one translation unit. Keep ordinary function definitions in a .c file.

references.title: A first GDB session
references.body: Build with -g and a low optimization level. break main sets a breakpoint; run starts; next steps over calls; step enters calls; print inspects a value; backtrace shows active frames.
references.example:
gdb ./app
(gdb) break main
(gdb) run
(gdb) next
(gdb) print total

references.title: Sanitizers give evidence, not proof
references.body: ASan and UBSan detect supported errors on executed paths. An error-free run does not establish correctness, portability, determinism, or absence of all memory bugs.

references.title: Three behavior categories
references.body: Undefined: no requirements for that execution. Unspecified: permitted alternatives without a documented choice requirement. Implementation-defined: a permitted choice the implementation must document.
references.example: signed overflow: undefined; argument evaluation order: unspecified; plain char signedness: implementation-defined

references.title: Optional C23 note
references.body: C17 is the baseline for this course, not the latest standard. C23 adds language features, including binary integer constants and nullptr. Compiler support is feature-specific; check official support documentation and use an explicit dialect. Do not use these features in C17 submissions.
references.example:
C17: -std=c17
C23 experiments: use a supported compiler and an explicit C23 flag

references.title: Long and size_t formats
references.body: Match the format to the argument type. %ld prints long, %zu prints size_t, %d prints int, %u prints unsigned int, and %.2f prints a double with two fractional digits. A char argument is promoted to int for %c.

references.title: calloc and initialized integers
references.body: calloc(count, size) allocates space for count objects of size bytes and initializes their bytes to zero. For integer objects this represents zero; do not generalize that claim to every pointer or floating-point representation. Check NULL and count/size arithmetic.

references.title: strlen requires a valid string
references.body: strlen counts bytes before the first NUL and returns size_t. It does not know capacity and cannot safely find the length of an unterminated character array. Validate that a terminator exists within readable bounds before treating arbitrary bytes as a string.

references.title: memcpy copies a known byte count
references.body: memcpy(dest, source, count) copies count bytes between nonoverlapping regions. Both regions must be valid for that count. For overlapping movement use memmove instead; our owned-copy examples allocate independent storage.
references.example: memcpy(copy, source, length + 1); /* known string length, including NUL */

references.title: Find a character with strchr
references.body: strchr searches a valid NUL-terminated string for a character and returns its address or NULL. It can locate the retained newline after fgets. Check the result before assigning through it.

references.title: fgetc and EOF
references.body: fgetc returns int, not char: its value can represent a read unsigned-char value or EOF. If it returns EOF, ferror distinguishes a read failure from ordinary end-of-file. Store the return in int before testing.
references.example: int next = fgetc(stdin); if (next == EOF) { /* inspect ferror(stdin) */ }

references.title: Character classification needs a safe argument
references.body: isspace from <ctype.h> accepts EOF or a value representable as unsigned char. Cast a character byte to unsigned char before passing it; a negative signed-char value otherwise violates the function contract.

references.title: Implicit function declaration
references.body: In modern C, declare a function before calling it. A library call normally needs its documented header; a custom call needs a matching prototype. Do not invent a prototype for a standard function or ignore the diagnostic.

references.title: Format argument mismatch
references.body: A printf conversion must match the actual promoted argument type. %d expects int, %ld long, %zu size_t, and %f double. A warning about a format mismatch describes a genuine contract problem, not merely a cosmetic issue.

references.title: Unused variables are a clue
references.body: An unused-variable warning can reveal a forgotten calculation, mistaken variable name, or unnecessary value. Decide whether the program should use the variable or remove it; do not suppress evidence blindly.
references.example: int total = 0; /* compute and report it, or remove it if unnecessary */

references.title: Signed overflow is not wrapping
references.body: In C17 signed integer overflow is undefined behavior. Check representable bounds before evaluating the risky expression. Unsigned arithmetic has modulo rules, but changing a type does not automatically satisfy an application contract.
references.example: if (b > 0 && a > INT_MAX - b) { /* reject before a + b */ }
